# ait

> ait is a local control plane and Git-native attempt ledger for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Aider, Gemini CLI, and Cursor. It gives AI coding agents repo-local memory, long-term attempt history, agent-to-agent handoff through `AIT_CONTEXT_FILE`, adversarial review, and reviewable attempts with explicit apply/recover flow on top of Git. Open source (MIT), Python 3.11+, dependency-free, no SaaS, no telemetry. Metadata is stored locally under `.ait/` next to `.git/`. The package is named `ait-vcs` on PyPI and npm; the installed command is `ait`.

ait is not an agent and not a Git replacement. It is the local control plane around AI coding agents: not merely a worktree manager, not a generic memory layer, not a review bot, and not a SaaS provenance dashboard. Every wrapped agent run produces one "attempt" record linking intent -> prompt -> context files -> exit status -> edited files -> resulting commits -> memory -> review evidence, queryable via a structured DSL. `ait status <adapter>` reports wrapper bypass risk so users can see whether the current shell will enter AIT or silently call the real agent binary. `ait graph --format json` emits the versioned `ait.work_graph` data contract, and `ait console --read-only` renders that data as a local read-only daily console; `ait console action ... --dry-run` records preflight and append-only journal entries, but browser mutation UI and action execution are not shipped. Repo-local memory is attempt-derived, evidence-backed project memory and an asynchronous handoff channel, not hidden chat memory, not an external vector database, and not a `CLAUDE.md` generator. AIT-owned memory under `.ait/` stores prior attempts, prior commits, curated notes, accepted facts, prior findings, and review findings, while live external sources such as `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/memory.md`, `.codex/memory.md`, and `.cursor/rules` are read at recall/run/review time and remain their own source of truth. Wrapped runs receive `AIT_CONTEXT_FILE` plus a versioned `ait.context_manifest`, so Claude Code, Codex, Aider, Gemini, Cursor, and shell agents can pick up policy-allowed context from one another without sharing a private chat transcript; candidate, stale, superseded, and policy-blocked memory is not trusted baseline, and policy-blocked body text is not copied into the context or manifest. `ait memory sources` and default `ait memory recall` are zero-touch reads. `ait memory backfill --dry-run` previews existing repo-local agent memory without writing; `backfill --import` is an explicit mutation/deprecated path that adds advisory memory under `.ait/`, and global or out-of-repo memory requires an explicit `--global --path`. Failed attempts stay isolated in their own worktree until you recover or discard them; successful changes only reach the current branch when you call `ait apply`. `.ait/policy.json` can be validated with fail-closed `ait policy validate`; `ait metadata export/import` currently emits dry-run local plans only, with no sync, telemetry, automatic push, or automatic merge.

## Core docs

- [Home](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/): overview, install, problems solved
- [Why ait](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/why-ait/): the ten problems ait solves (blast radius, provenance, parallel agents, explicit apply, agent-to-agent communication, local-first, review evidence, prompt search)
- [Pain-point demos](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/demos/pain-point-demos/): Claude Code and Codex scenario commands for every problem on the Why ait page, including isolation, provenance, context handoff, explicit apply, local-only metadata, review evidence, and prompt search. The repository also provides an executable suite under `examples/pain-point-demos` with `setup.sh` plus one `run.sh` per pain point.
- [Getting started](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/getting-started/): install ait-vcs, run `ait init`, check wrapper bypass status, run first wrapped agent, inspect live memory sources, apply the attempt
- [Command reference](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/reference/commands/): all `ait` subcommands — init, status and bypass detection, doctor, adapter, attempt, intent, context, memory sources/recall/backfill, review, review benchmark, graph, console, policy, metadata, repair, upgrade, shell
- [Live federated memory](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/reference/live-federated-memory/): zero-touch live source discovery and recall, source/status/trust model, false-memory and stale-memory executable fixture scope, context manifests, external source-of-truth boundaries, and explicit mutation paths
- [Review modes](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/reference/review-modes/): exact boundaries for `light`, `adversarial`, `risk-based`, local `claude -p` reviewer execution, and policy-gated memory baselines
- [Adversarial code review](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/reference/adversarial-code-review/): end-to-end reviewer workflow — risk scan, Claude Code reviewer adapter, custom command adapters, findings, reports, and review-gated apply decisions
- [AI search facts](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/facts/): self-contained Q&A — what is ait, how it differs from git-worktree, install, supported agents, privacy, safety boundaries

## Integrations

- [Claude Code](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/integrations/claude-code/): wrap `claude` in a worktree; `ait init` auto-installs the wrapper and merges SessionStart/PostToolUse/SessionEnd hooks into `.claude/settings.json`; the `claude-code` adversarial reviewer uses local `claude -p` and strips `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from that child process
- [Codex CLI](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/integrations/codex/): native `.codex/hooks.json` bridge with full transcript capture
- [Aider](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/integrations/aider/): post-run `.aider.chat.history.md` conversion to attempt transcript
- [Gemini CLI](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/integrations/gemini/): native `.gemini/settings.json` hook bridge
- [Cursor](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/integrations/cursor/): captures `cursor-agent --print --output-format stream-json` stream
- [Generic shell agent](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/integrations/shell/): `ait run --adapter shell -- <any command>` for custom agents

## Comparisons

- [ait vs naked git-worktree](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/compare/git-worktree-naked-vs-ait/): when manual worktrees suffice and when they break down
- [ait vs agent managers, memory layers, and review bots](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/compare/agent-managers-memory-review-vs-ait/): category boundary against GUI-first agent managers, worktree managers, memory layers, review bots, and provenance tools
